sources.news_title: US Marine Accused of Murdering, Robbing Japanese Woman
sources.text:
A U.S. Marine based in Okinawa was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture.
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, a 20-year-old stationed at the Futenma Air Station, is suspected of killing 39-year-old Anna Yagi inside a hotel on Saturday, according to the Okinawa Prefectural Police Department.
Police said security camera footage allegedly showed him entering the hotel with the victim and exiting alone with her wallet and backpack in the early morning hours of Oct. 3.
The Kyodo News agency reported that the victim’s body was found after she appeared to have been strangled in her hotel room.
Ballard denied the allegations against him, police said.
An investigation into the events surrounding the night is still underway.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi expressed her condolences to the victim’s family in a Sunday post on X.
“The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret, and as the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side, while firmly demanding maximum cooperation with the investigation, strict discipline among U.S. military personnel, and thorough measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents and accidents,” Takaichi wrote.
Takaichi added that the government plans to address the case with “the utmost care and diligence.”
Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi called the incident unacceptable.
“I am deeply outraged,” Koizumi said in comments that aired on Japan’s national broadcaster NHK.
First Lt. Tyler N. Thomas, a spokesperson for the III Marine Expeditionary Force, confirmed in a statement on Oct. 3 that the United States was actively cooperating with Japanese authorities.
“We extend our deepest condolences to the victim’s family and friends,” Thomas added.
“The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior.”
Thomas, who did not name Ballard in the statement, said the Marine was in custody during the investigation and did not have additional information to release.
The Epoch Times reached out to the III Marine Expeditionary Force for additional information.
Around 18,000 Marines based in Japan are stationed in Okinawa, which has been a sensitive issue for locals over the course of many decades.
In 2017, a Japanese court in Naha convicted Kenneth Shinzato, a former Marine and U.S. military contractor, of murder and rape charges in the death of an Okinawa woman and sentenced him to life in prison.
In 1995, mass protests occurred after three U.S. servicemen raped a 12-year-old Okinawan girl. The men were sentenced to more than 6 years in prison.

sources.text:

Japanese authorities took Devin Jacob Ballard into custody after the body of 39-year-old Anna Yagi was discovered in a Naha hotel room early Saturday, the Daily Mail reported.
Police suspect the killing happened between 2 and 4 a.m. Emergency crews were called around 4:20 a.m. and pronounced Yagi dead at the scene.
Ballard is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and has been stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma on Okinawa. He faces suspicion of both murder and robbery while the investigation continues under Japanese control.
Yagi did not check out on time. A hotel worker unlocked the door and found her unresponsive inside the room.
Security footage reviewed by police showed a man and woman entering the hotel together. The man later walked out alone, carrying the woman’s belongings. Officers initially hunted for an unidentified suspect after studying that video.
Belongings linked to Yagi turned up around the hotel. Police then arrested Ballard on suspicion of robbery and murder. Japanese outlet Asahi identified the Marine by name; local media carried the same identification.
Breitbart reported police believe Yagi was killed by neck suffocation. The outlet also noted that Japanese officials lodged a formal protest with the U.S. government over the case.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the incident extremely regrettable and demanded full cooperation from American authorities.
A Marines spokesperson based in Okinawa issued a statement stressing both accountability and condolences.
"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force. We extend our deepest condolences to the victim's family and friends."
The same spokesperson added a second point on standards and custody.
"The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior. The Marine is in custody of local authorities while the investigation proceeds."
Okinawa hosts a large American military footprint, including the III Marine Expeditionary Force and the Futenma air station network. That presence support the U.S.-Japan alliance. It also places every service member under intense local scrutiny when serious crimes are alleged.
Authorities have not released the exact forensic cause of death beyond the neck-suffocation account carried in supporting coverage. The nature of any prior connection between Ballard and Yagi remains unclear. The specific hotel has not been named in the available reporting. No formal charging statutes or case numbers beyond the stated suspicion of robbery and murder have been detailed publicly.
What is established is straightforward: a Japanese civilian died in a Naha hotel room, surveillance captured a man leaving with her property, and a 20-year-old Marine now sits in local custody while Japanese police work the case and Tokyo presses Washington for full cooperation.

sources.news_title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of murder after 'brutal and heinous' death in Japan, officials say
sources.text:
Officials in Japan said they lodged a "strong" protest with the United States.
A U.S. service member was arrested on suspicion of murder and robbery after a Japanese woman's body was discovered in a hotel in Okinawa, local officials said, describing the alleged killing as a "heinous" incident that prompted the Japanese government to lodge a protest with the United States.
Shinjiro Koizumi, the Japanese minister of defense, said a U.S. Marine lance corporal was arrested on Sunday after the woman's body was found early on Saturday in Naha, the capital city of the Okinawa prefecture.
NHK, Japan's public broadcaster, identified the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at U.S. Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, a base a few miles outside Naha. The broadcaster identified the alleged victim as Yagi Anna, 39, saying she was pronounced dead at the scene after being found at about 4:30 a.m. on Saturday.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the Okinawa Prefectural Police were investigating the incident as a murder.
"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret, and as the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side," she said on social media.
NHK reported that security camera footage showed a person who "appeared to be foreign entering the hotel with a woman and later leaving with her belongings." Some of Yagi's belongings were allegedly found abandoned near the hotel, NKH reported, citing local police.
The hair and tattoos of the person in the security camera footage reportedly resemble Ballard's, according to NHK, which also reported that he is suspected of killing Anna between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. local time Saturday and stealing her wallet and other unspecified belongings. Ballard was located late Saturday night in an entertainment district in Okinawa City, about 18 kilometers away from the hotel, and was arrested, according to NHK.
Anna's cause of death was suffocation caused by pressure on her neck, NHK reports police saying. Ballard has denied killing Anna, police said, according to NHK.
U.S. officials did not immediately confirm the identity of the service member who was arrested, nor did they say whether the person had been officially charged in connection with the death.
"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force," the force said in a statement on social media. "We extend our deepest condolences to the victim's family and friends."
Tens of thousands of U.S. troops are stationed across Japan, including in the country's southernmost prefecture, Okinawa, which is home to several U.S. bases.
The U.S. Embassy in Tokyo said it was aware of the incident and was extending "our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased."
"At present, an investigation is underway to clarify the facts, and the United States Government continues to cooperate closely with the Government of Japan and local authorities," the embassy said in a statement.
George Glass, the U.S. ambassador to Japan, said he had spoken on Sunday morning with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Okinawa's governor, adding that his office was providing full cooperation with an investigation into the death.
The office of Toshimitsu Motegi, Japan's foreign minister, said it had summoned Glass on Sunday to issue a protest.
Motegi "strongly urged the U.S. side to strengthen discipline and to prevent the recurrence of incidents so that such a tragedy will never be repeated," his office said in a press release.
Okinawa Gov. Genta Koja called on Sunday for the U.S. military in Japan to "rigorously enforce discipline among its service members."
"As Okinawa Prefecture, we will deal with this strictly, including by lodging strong protests with the U.S. military and both the Japanese and U.S. governments, to ensure that such tragic incidents never happen again," he said in a statement.
ABC News' Rashid Haddou and Joe Simonetti contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Japan PM Protests US Marine Arrest in Okinawa as Police Probe Suspected Robbery-Murder at Hotel
sources.text:
Japan PM Protests US Marine Arrest in Okinawa as Police Probe Suspected Robbery-Murder at Hotel
The 20-year-old serviceman denies the allegations as Japanese and US authorities investigate the death of a 39-year-old woman in Naha
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has lodged a strong protest with the United States after a 20-year-old US Marine was arrested on suspicion of murder and robbery in Okinawa. The arrest followed the discovery of a 39-year-old woman's body in a hotel room in Naha early on Saturday.
Okinawa police said the woman was found unresponsive at about 4.30am local time and was pronounced dead at the scene. Police told reporters that the condition of her body suggested she had been murdered, although investigators have not released further details.
The Marine was arrested at about 1am on Sunday while walking through Naha, police said. He was stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, also on Okinawa, according to the force.
Takaichi Lodges Strong Protest Over Incident
Takaichi said the Japanese Government had lodged a strong protest with the US over the incident, describing it as 'extremely brutal and heinous.'
'The Government of Japan has strongly protested to the US side and has called for the fullest possible cooperation with the investigation, thorough discipline among US military personnel, and comprehensive measures to prevent a recurrence of crimes and accidents,' she said in a statement posted on X.
The Government's response goes beyond the immediate criminal investigation, with Tokyo also calling for stronger discipline among US military personnel and measures to prevent similar incidents. It is also pressing Washington over military discipline, against a backdrop of longstanding political tension surrounding the US military presence in Okinawa.
Police said CCTV footage reportedly showed a man believed to be a foreign national entering the hotel room with the woman and later leaving the building with her belongings.
Those details remain part of an active investigation. The Marine has been arrested on suspicion, not convicted, and has denied the allegations. The available information does not establish what happened inside the room.
The US Marine Corps said it had extended its condolences to the woman's family. It added that it took the allegations 'very seriously' and expected every Marine to maintain the highest standards of behaviour.
'We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force,' the service stated.
The US Embassy in Tokyo also confirmed that an American service member was in custody following the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa. The embassy said the US was communicating and co-operating with Japanese authorities while investigators worked to determine the facts.
Why the Protest Matters in Okinawa
Okinawa hosts a substantial part of the US military presence in Japan and is regarded by Tokyo and Washington as strategically important. That arrangement has also produced repeated friction with local residents, particularly when crimes or accidents involve American personnel.
The most notorious case came in 1995, when three US servicemen raped a 12-year-old girl. The crime triggered widespread anger and mass protests across Okinawa, intensifying opposition to the military presence and placing renewed pressure on Tokyo and Washington.
That history has linked allegations involving US troops to broader debates over accountability, the burden of military bases and the effectiveness of measures intended to address local concerns.
Still, investigators have so far offered only limited information. Police have not publicly detailed the suspected motive, the nature of the alleged robbery or the evidence linking the arrested Marine to the woman's death beyond the information attributed to the investigation.
The case is therefore at an early and legally sensitive stage. The arrest does not by itself establish that the suspect committed murder or robbery. Investigators are still working to establish what happened and what evidence supports the allegations.
Japanese authorities will need to establish the sequence of events, the circumstances of the woman's death and what significance the reported CCTV footage has to the investigation.
The Marine Corps and the US Embassy have both said they are co-operating. Takaichi also called for stronger discipline among US military personnel and measures to prevent a recurrence.
The case has already prompted anger in Okinawa, where the presence of US troops has long been politically sensitive. The case could add to longstanding political tensions surrounding the US military presence in Okinawa.
For now, though, the central questions remain with the police, and with the evidence still being examined.

The employee unlocked the door at the Naminoue Crystal Hotel in Naha’s Wakasa district after Anna Yagi, 39, of Naha, failed to leave by the designated checkout time. That failure brought a staff member to the room. The employee unlocked the door and found Yagi unconscious.
Emergency services were called around 4:20 a.m. on Saturday, October 3, 2026. Yagi was pronounced dead at the scene. Police placed her death between 2:10 a.m. and 4:17 a.m.
Okinawa prefectural police had a body at the hotel, a Naha woman past checkout, and a death timed in those early hours.
Police pulled the hotel surveillance. The cameras showed a man and a woman entering the Naminoue Crystal Hotel together. Later the same cameras recorded the man leaving alone, carrying belongings that investigators said were hers. Police alleged a wallet and a backpack, or another item with them, had been taken. Those belongings turned up afterward scattered around the hotel.
Before any name attached to the image, the description went out from the footage alone. The man had a shaved head or a close buzz cut. He wore a black tank top, three-quarter-length pants, and white sneakers. Authorities treated the unidentified man as someone who could have information about what had happened inside the room and opened an urgent search for anyone matching that look.
The hunt ran on the sequence the cameras had fixed: the pair walking in, the man walking out alone with the items in hand, the scattered belongings recovered on the grounds. Late Saturday night the search was still open when a police officer moved through Naha’s entertainment district.
He stopped a man walking alone on a street there. The officer questioned the man where he stood and then detained him. Police identified him as Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard. He was 20 years old. He was a United States Marine stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma. Lance corporal is an enlisted rank in the Marine Corps, the step above private first class and below corporal. Genta Koja, “offering our sincere condolences and pledging full cooperation as the investigation continues.” U.S. Embassy Tokyo wrote on X the same day: “We are aware that a US service member is in custody following the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa. Further enquiries were under way to establish the full sequence of events at the Naminoue Crystal Hotel.

A United States Marine was arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, Japan, police said Sunday, prompting an official protest from the Japanese government.
The 20-year-old lance corporal is suspected of robbing and murdering a 39-year-old woman in a hotel in Naha, the capital of Japan's most southernmost prefecture.

The suspect reportedly denies the charges.
What have Japanese officials said?
"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and vicious incident is extremely regrettable," said Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a statement as Tokyo registered an official protest with Washington.
"The government of Japan strongly protests to the US side and strongly seeks maximum cooperation with the investigation," she continued, also calling for "stricter discipline among US military personnel" and "thorough measures" to prevent a recurrence.

Okinawa itself has an enormous American military presence and is home to III Marine Expeditionary Force and Marine Corps Installations Pacific, along with a network of Marine Corps installations.
The US military presence on the island means thousands of American service personnel are stationed in the region.
The Daily Mail has contacted the Marines and the Department of War for comment.
The Okinawa Prefectural Police have also been contacted for further details.
